candidates.name: Palácio da Bolsa
candidates.content: It was built in the 19th century on the grounds of the destroyed old cloisters of the adjacent São Francisco church. It also contains the most impressive Arab room in the country. There is also a Port wine tasting room.

candidates.name: Sé do Porto
candidates.price: €3. Combined ticket with adjacent Bishop's palace €6
candidates.content: This Romanesque cathedral was built in the 13th century. Later on Baroque alterations were made in the 17th and 18th century. The cathedral is on top of a hill from where you also have great views over the city and the river.

candidates.name: Fundação de Serralves
candidates.price: €8.50 museum and park, €4 park only. 50% discount for 65+ and Porto card holders. Free on Sundays 10:00-13:00 for students and under 18
candidates.content: A contemporary museum designed by the famous architect Álvaro Siza, with a huge garden/park and an Art Deco Villa. When visiting this foundation you can visit the exhibitions, relax at the park, have lunch at the restaurant, bar o

candidates.name: Port Wine Institute
candidates.content: A small exhibition about Port wine and its certification process. Samples of a small variety of Port wines can be bought. Guided tastings and tours to the laboratories can be arranged.

candidates.name: Igreja de São Francisco
candidates.content: A Gothic church with later alterations of the interior decorations in Baroque style.

candidates.name: Mercado do Bolhão
candidates.content: A traditional market of fruits, vegetables, fish and meat. As of 2022 the entire market is now open after major refurbishment.

candidates.name: Livraria Lello
candidates.price: Due to the absurd number of tourists, to get in you have to buy a €10 ticket online (or €12 at the entrance), which can be used towards book purchases
candidates.content: It's an old bookshop with an amazing interior and spiral staircase. Voted as one of the most beautiful bookshops in Europe. Be warned that it can get incredibly crowded and claustrophobic.

candidates.name: Torre dos Clérigos
candidates.price: €8 (includes entry to a small exhibition at the lower levels of the tower)
candidates.content: Panoramic views from this baroque tower. 226 steps to the top. It is best to get there early since there is not a lot of space on the viewing platform. You might even have to wait for some time before you are allowed to climb up t

candidates.name: National Museum Soares dos Reis
candidates.content: Museum displaying Portuguese art. Founded in 1833.

candidates.name: Centro Português de Fotografia
candidates.content: Housed in a beautiful building in the centre of the city.

candidates.name: Ribeira
candidates.content: The part of the city near the river, which is also a good place to start visiting the World Heritage area; to the other side of the river you will see the Ribeira de Gaia, a similar area from the city of Vila Nova de Gaia (the two

candidates.name: Casa da Música
candidates.content: Designed by Rem Koolhaas and OMA. Guided tour available in English from 1 June - 30 September at 10:00, 11:00, 16:00 and 17:00 for €10/person (free for children under 12) which take about 1 hour. The rest of the year the guided to

candidates.name: Pavilhão Rosa Mota
candidates.content: A multi purpose pavilion with nice gardens to rest, also known as "Palácio de Cristal".

candidates.name: Museu Romântico
candidates.content: A house where the King of Italy stayed while in exile.

candidates.name: She Changes
candidates.content: Monumental public sculpture

candidates.name: Museum of Sacred Art and Archaeology of The Higher Seminary of Porto
Teatro Nacional São João (TNSJ)
candidates.content: Porto's main theatre and opera production company and venue. There are also guided tours (€5/person) for access to the stage, rehearsal room, dressing rooms and the technical area (if they are not used during the time of the tour)

candidates.name: Fado Bars
candidates.content: Fado is a music genre originating in Lisbon and considered an integral part of Portuguese music. It is traditionally sung by a woman in a black dress, accompanied by guitar players. A handful of Fado bars stand in Porto, primarily

candidates.name: FC Porto
candidates.content: They play in Primeira Liga, Portugal's top tier. Their home ground Estádio do Dragão (capacity 50,000) is 1 km north of the centre with its own metro station.

candidates.name: Boavista FC
candidates.content: They were relegated in 2025 and now play in Liga 2 the second tier. Their Estádio do Bessa (capacity 28,200) is 2 km northwest of the centre, metro Francos.

candidates.name: Douro river cruise
candidates.content: Take a cruise upriver (the cost starts at €15 (although they can be slightly cheaper if paired with a different activity) and takes about 50 minutes. Cruises run from 10:00 to 18:30, with sailings every 30 minutes for most operato

candidates.name: Porto Exit Games
candidates.content: You're locked in a room with a mystery to solve and the clock ticking. Can you crack the puzzle and escape?

candidates.name: Discoteca Via Rápida
candidates.content: A popular disco in the Industrial Area. The nightclub opens Fridays and Saturdays and it's always crowded. The club plays the latest dance hits and the crowd is 20ish.

candidates.name: Prioridade Bar
candidates.content: In the Ribeira region, this bar is one of the cheapest in the area. It's probably the only decent place in the whole of the Ribeira region (and probably, in the city) where you can get a large beer for only a few euros. They also

candidates.name: Industria
candidates.content: "Local heroes and international superstars" - going since 1987. It's open until around 06:00.

candidates.name: Passos Manuel
candidates.content: A dance club/bar frequented by the arty crowd, with a varied but tasteful selection of music and a warm decór.

candidates.name: Plano B
candidates.content: Near Torre dos Clérigos is a popular art gallery and bar installed on Porto's historic centre.

candidates.name: Clube Mau Mau
candidates.content: In the Foz region, it is a popular nightclub with varying musical styles, from house to pop to R&B.

candidates.name: Ryan's Irish Pub
candidates.content: In the Ribeira, nice cozy atmosphere and friendly bar staff. Always a good place to start.

candidates.name: Solar Vinho do Porto
candidates.content: Rua de Entre-Quintas 220. A villa with port samples and a great view of the Douro. Open M-Sa 14:00-00:00. This is the perfect place to sit in soft chairs or outside in the garden and enjoy a few glasses of the finest ports. You ca

candidates.name: Café Piolho / Âncora d'Ouro
candidates.content: The third oldest cafe in Porto, it is commonly known as "O Piolho" (the Louse). The cafe looks out on the street facing a faculty of the Universidade do Porto, and had been a meeting place for students since the 19th century. Plaq

candidates.name: Casa Das Tortas
candidates.content: Great authentic Portuguese food homemade with bakery pastries. A very good place to eat typical food. Best Francesinha in Porto.

candidates.name: Murça No Porto
candidates.content: A small and traditional restaurant typical of Porto, one of the few remaining true. Like eating a home cooked meal. Lots of locals are there.

candidates.name: Varanda Da Barra
candidates.content: Great restaurant that serves traditional Portuguese, Italian and "International" food. Nice riverside view.

candidates.name: Taberna Folias de Baco
candidates.content: A small cozy Portuguese restaurant with a nice ambiance. You can sip on amazing wine while eating delicious authentic food. The manager is very friendly and helpful.

candidates.name: Laurear
candidates.content: Authentic fabulous Portuguese food. Small and cozy place with very friendly service. It's rather small, you have to be lucky to get a table in the evening.

candidates.name: Taxca
candidates.content: A typical Portuguese tavern, with excellent quality gastronomy products, the atmosphere is fantastic, typical of a tavern, without table service, the hanging hams immediately whet your appetite. One of the best places to snack on

candidates.name: A Loja dos Pastéis de Chaves
candidates.content: Lovely eatery just off the main shopping street. Genuine food also suitable for vegetarians. The place is nice and chill. They have a really big menu with a lot of options.

candidates.name: O Comercial
candidates.content: Elegant atmosphere in the Palácio da Bolsa (Stock Exchange Palace). Large windows face the River Douro. They serve Portuguese cuisine tweaked with some new techniques and products.

candidates.name: Trinkas Petisqueira Lounge
candidates.content: Very good cuisine, simple, homemade and careful. Lovely little restaurant, great for sitting by the side of the road and watching the world go by.

candidates.name: Churrasqueira Brasil
candidates.content: Don’t let the outside appearance fool you. This place is a hidden gem. Great homemade food and attention. Very nice place to eat the dish of the day.

candidates.name: Taberna do Doutor
candidates.content: Fantastic francesinha and great sardines. Friendly and attentive staff.
